title: Deep Blue vs Kasparov, Game 6
summary: Game 6 is remembered as the game where Kasparov resigned after 19.c4, with Deep Blue's attack on the uncastled king and the bishop sacrifice on f5 deciding the result. Watch how the engine's evaluation climbs after the early inaccuracy at 7...h6, and how each sacrifice opens lines towards Black's king.

moves.comment: White claims the centre with the king's pawn, the most natural start and rated best by the engine.
A Caro-Kann style reply. The engine preferred 1...e5, which challenges the centre more directly.
White builds a broad pawn centre with d4, a classical and sound choice rated best.
Black strikes at the centre with 2...d5, a best move that slightly improves Black's evaluation.
Developing the knight to c3 is playable but only good. The engine preferred the pawn advance 3.e5.
Black captures on e4, releasing the tension and opening the d-file. Rated best.
White recaptures with the knight, restoring the balance and keeping the centre under control.
Black develops the knight to d7, covering e5 and preparing to bring the other knight to f6.
The knight jumps to g5, aiming at f7 and e6. The engine preferred 5.Bd3, so this is only good.
Black develops with 5...Ngf6, hitting the knight on e4 and keeping the position solid. Rated best.
The bishop comes to d3, supporting the knight on e4 and eyeing the kingside. A best move.
Black opens lines for the bishop on f8 with 6...e6. A best move that keeps the position stable.
White develops the last minor piece with 7.Nf3, adding pressure on e5 and keeping development smooth.
The pawn move 7...h6 is an inaccuracy. The engine preferred 7...Bd6, and the evaluation jumps from +0.3 to +1.1.

moment.title: A quiet pawn move
moment.text: The pawn move 7...h6 looks harmless, yet the engine rates it an inaccuracy. The evaluation jumps from +0.3 to +1.1 in one move. Notice how the bishop on d6 would have kept the position under control.

moves.comment: White takes the e6 pawn with the knight. Rated best, and the evaluation rises to +1.3.
Black avoids recapturing at once with 8...Qe7. The engine preferred 8...fxe6, and the evaluation climbs to +1.9.
White castles, bringing the rook towards the centre and the e-file. A best move that lifts the evaluation to +2.1.
Black recaptures with the f-pawn, winning the knight for a pawn. The engine still shows White ahead at +2.2, reflecting the open king.

moment.title: Black wins a knight for a pawn
moment.text: After 8.Nxe6 Qe7 9.O-O fxe6, Black has won the knight for a pawn. The engine still shows White ahead at +2.2, which reflects the open king and the pressure on the f-file. Material alone does not tell the whole story here.

moves.comment: Bishop check on g6 along the diagonal to e8. Rated best and keeps the king under immediate pressure.

moment.title: Bishop check opens the king
moment.text: 10.Bg6+ forces the king to move and keeps the attack going. Black's king is stuck in the centre with open lines. Watch how each White move aims at the king rather than at material.

moves.comment: The king steps aside to d8. This is the sensible escape, rated best.
The bishop retreats to f4, keeping pressure on the position and staying active. A best move.
Black plays 11...b5 for queenside space. The engine preferred 11...Nh7, and the evaluation rises to +2.6.
White hits the b5 pawn with a4, opening lines on the queenside. The engine preferred 12.Bg3, so this is only good.
Black develops the bishop to b7. Good, though the engine preferred 12...a5, and the evaluation edges up to +2.8.
The rook joins the e-file, adding force against Black's centre. A best move.
The knight centralises on d5, a best move, although the evaluation climbs to +3.0.
The bishop returns to g3, a best move that lowers the evaluation slightly to +2.7.
The king moves to c8, an inaccuracy. The engine preferred 14...a5, and the evaluation jumps to +3.7.

moment.title: The king move that cost the balance
moment.text: 14...Kc8 is an inaccuracy, and the evaluation jumps from +2.7 to +3.7. The engine preferred 14...a5 to challenge White's queenside play. The king on c8 stays exposed to the a-file.

moves.comment: White captures on b5, opening the a-file towards Black's king. A best move that keeps the evaluation near +3.6.
Black recaptures with the c-pawn, keeping the queenside structure intact. Rated best.
The queen comes to d3, a good move. The engine preferred 16.Rc1 to bring another piece into the attack.
Black develops the bishop to c6. Good, but the engine preferred 16...a6, and the evaluation rises to +4.0.
White offers the bishop with 17.Bf5, a good move. The engine preferred 17.Rec1, though the attack remains strong.
Black accepts the bishop with 17...exf5. The best reply, and the evaluation is +4.3.
The rook takes the queen on e7, a best move that wins decisive material and raises the evaluation to +4.6.

moment.title: The rook takes the queen
moment.text: After the bishop sacrifice on f5, 18.Rxe7 wins the queen for a rook. The evaluation climbs to +4.6, and the attack has become decisive. Notice how the sacrifice was used to remove the defending queen.

moves.comment: Black recaptures with the bishop. This is an inaccuracy; the engine preferred 18...Nxe7, and the evaluation jumps to +6.2.

moment.title: Recapture that gave up the advantage
moment.text: 18...Bxe7 is an inaccuracy, and the evaluation rises from +4.6 to +6.2. The engine preferred 18...Nxe7 to keep the knight active. The move confirmed that Black's position had no defence left.

moves.comment: White plays 19.c4, a best move that pushes the evaluation to +6.7. Kasparov resigned after this move.

lessons: Before playing a quiet pawn move, check whether it weakens squares around your king, as 7...h6 did here.
When you give up material for an attack, count the open lines and the checks you can make before you commit.
Look for a sacrifice that removes the defender of the king, because a rook taking a queen can decide the game.
